sonnet.problem: The statement says the ark is 'still' to be carried on their shoulders. Verse 3 only says 'It is not to be carried around on your shoulders.' The word 'still' implies they had been carrying it, which the text doesn't say.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. / Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: This is a 'for whom' question, but both wrong answers ('The royal bodyguards', 'The visiting envoys') are invented. They are not real details from somewhere in the Bible.
sonnet.rule: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

sonnet.problem: The story card has 3 sentences. It also goes item by item through the officials and their animal counts instead of summing up the stretch in a few words.
sonnet.rule: Every other story card, including the first card of a later stop, is 1 to 2 sentences. / He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

sonnet.problem: This is a 'who' question, but both wrong answers ('The royal servants', 'The temple guards') are invented. They are not real details from somewhere in the Bible. The question also adds the setting 'at the altar', which verse 14 doesn't give.
sonnet.rule: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. / No added settings. No setting the text doesn't give.

sonnet.problem: Card 7 already asked who 'makes preparations' for the priests and revealed the Levites do it. This card's right answer, 'Others make preparations for them', is the same fact and the same phrase, so the earlier card gives it away and the question re-asks it.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. / An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'this one' with no context. The story card before it isn't on screen, so the baker can't tell whose Passover is meant (Josiah's).
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never 'him,' 'that' or 'it' pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: Card 12's question already states that no Passover like this one has happened since Samuel's days. That gives away this card's answer, that no earlier king observed one like it. Both cards also make the same point from verse 18.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. / Two lines that make the same point get one question.
